findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and are cancelled
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx,...)` where ctx is the request context. When the handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the child context is immediately cancelled and the async Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection fails with context canceled. Mode 3's safety backup to legacy therefore never happens. Fix by detaching with context.WithoutCancel/background plus timeout.

findings.title: Legacy create replicates input object instead of storage result
findings.body: Create returns `created` from Storage but async replication calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original input `obj`. Storage-assigned fields like generated names, UID, resourceVersion and defaults are lost. For generateName creates the two stores will generate different names and diverge, corrupting the legacy backup. Should replicate `created` (deep copy) and not share caller-owned `obj` pointer with an async goroutine.

findings.title: Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergent writes
findings.body: Update calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same objInfo. Each store internally calls `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own old object, so the transformer runs twice against different old objects and can produce different results or resourceVersion conflicts. The old code fetched the updated object once and reused it via updateWrapper for both stores. Reusing objInfo breaks atomic dual-write consistency.

findings.title: Storage duration metric uses object name as kind label
findings.body: Delete success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` where `name` is the object name, while all other calls pass `options.Kind`. If the third parameter is the kind label, passing user-controlled object names creates unbounded Prometheus label cardinality and can OOM the metrics system. Should be `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Storage and legacy metrics recorded with wrong function
findings.body: On Storage.Create failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, on Storage.Update failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, and on async legacy DeleteCollection it calls `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Failures are attributed to the wrong store, hiding unified-storage errors and legacy replication errors from dashboards and alerts. Each should record for the store that actually failed.

findings.title: Async legacy failures are never logged
findings.body: All four async legacy branches only call `recordLegacyDuration/recordStorageDuration` and discard the error without `log.Error`. Operators have no log line to diagnose why legacy and unified storage diverged in mode 3, unlike the previous synchronous code that logged. Should log the legacy error with object identity.

findings.title: Delete puts wrong logger in context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. The enriched fields are dropped from the context while Create/Update/List/DeleteCollection propagate the enriched logger, making Delete logs inconsistent and harder to correlate.

findings.title: Mode3 unit tests do not verify async legacy writes
findings.body: Tests share one `mock.Mock` for both legacy and storage mocks, set up only storage expectations for Delete/DeleteCollection, and return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine. They cannot prove legacy was or was not called, cannot catch panics from missing mock expectations in the goroutine, and pass even if async replication is broken. Need separate mocks plus Eventually/AssertCalled for legacy.

findings.title: Mode3 integration tests assume synchronous legacy consistency
findings.body: The new file/unified mode-3 subtests reuse `doPlaylistTests` which does immediate `getFromBothAPIs` and legacy list checks right after k8s Create/Update. Since mode 3 replicates to legacy asynchronously with up to 10s timeout, the legacy read can race and the test will be flaky or falsely fail. Needs retry/eventual-consistency polling for legacy assertions in mode 3.
